monte_carlo.timestep_note: Terminal-value sampling: ONE timestep per path. A 252-step path-dependent simulation does ~252x the work per path, so this paths/sec figure is NOT comparable to a path-dependent one.
monte_carlo.rng: std::mt19937_64, per-block substreams seeded by splitmix64(seed+block)
monte_carlo.eight_physical_core_note: NOT MEASURED. This host has 2 physical cores (4 logical). No 8-core number is reported and none is extrapolated -- run this harness on an 8-core host and it will populate automatically.
monte_carlo.smt_note: Rows with oversubscribed_smt=true run more threads than physical cores. SMT shares execution units, so those rows are NOT evidence of per-core scaling and must not be extrapolated from.

connectivity.end_to_end_note: tick validate -> book update -> top-of-book read -> pre-trade risk -> NewOrderSingle encode, single thread, in-process. EXCLUDES network, kernel and venue time, which dominate real wire-to-wire latency.

methodology: Each figure runs a warm-up call, then repeats until a >=0.35s time floor to stay clear of clock resolution. ops/sec = total ops / elapsed wall time on an otherwise-loaded desktop OS with no CPU pinning, no isolated cores and no hugepages -- treat these as relative comparisons between implementations on this host, not as absolute production latency figures.
